code: const std::string original(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(data), size); auto input = std::string(original.c_str());
note: Attacker-controlled bytes after the 2-byte header become the JSON input string passed to the parser.
The JSON string is passed to Parser::ParseJson, which invokes DoParseJson and then ParseTable on the root Monster table.

code: Value val = field->value; ... ECHECK(ParseAnyValue(val, field, fieldn, struct_def_inner, 0));
note: For each JSON field, ParseAnyValue populates val.constant with the raw attribute string from the JSON token.
TryTypedValue assigns the raw token text (e.g. a float literal) to e.constant, which later becomes field_value.constant.
The raw constant string is converted to a scalar via atot. If the string is an out-of-range or malformed numeric literal, atot may fail.

code: auto done = atot_scalar(s, val, bool_constant<is_floating_point<T>::value>()); if (done) return NoError(); if (0 == *val)
note: When atot_scalar returns false, the code reads *val to decide which error message to produce. If StringToNumber failed without initializing *val, this read is a use-of-uninitialized-value.
For int64_t, StringToNumber delegates to StringToIntegerImpl with check_errno=true. On errno overflow, it returns false without explicitly writing *val after strtoll already set it.

When strtoll/strtoull sets errno=ERANGE for an out-of-range value, this path returns false. The value written by strtoll is implementation-defined and may be partially uninitialized under MSAN for certain inputs.
MSAN flags the read of *val here as use-of-uninitialized-value when the conversion failed via the errno path and the underlying libc did not fully initialize the output.
The uninitialized read propagates back through ECHECK, causing the MSAN crash in the monster_fuzzer target.
